blocking_unknown: Pointer relocation is REFLECTION-DRIVEN, not a flat table (finding igz.loader.relocation-table, static probe igz relocation-probe): no flat/bitmap/delta encoding in any section reproduces the 162 110 relocated words (best recall < 2%), there is no named fixup section, and a structural model (per-type fixed pointer fields + variable-length pointer arrays) explains 76%. Each type carries field descriptors that the loader walks per object to rebase pointers. Reframed M3 path: there is no flat list to extend; a clone of an existing type needs no new relocation data, only to be PROCESSED by the per-type field walk (a header-table entry). The two open sub-tasks are (a) locate the per-type field descriptors in the section-0 metadata to model relocation to 100%, and (b) register the clone without the global 32-byte shift that desynchronised the load when the header table was grown.
mechanism_found: Why a valid appended IGZ object is not instantiated: (1) the loader does not walk section 1 sequentially, does not use the header table as a construction root and does not use the section-0 table as a size stream; it constructs a contiguous span of records and each record builds its embedded children (findings igz.loader.enumerated-span, igz.loader.pointer-traversal). (2) An object appended after the last record is outside the span and stays raw bytes (never constructed) — the cause of the first M3 failure. (3) Loading applies a fixup pass: section-indexed pointers (igz.pointer.section-indexed), class pointers, id remap, reference counts (igz.object.refcount); section 5 is a second object section with 2 320 pointers into section 1 (igz.section5.object-section).
